subject: Request: Short-term rate smoothing to offset prefetch regression impact
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Short-term rate smoothing to offset prefetch regression impact

Samantha —

Thanks again for raising the spike you saw last week. We dug into the logs with infra and confirmed a prefetch optimization we shipped in late May regresses token emission patterns for your workflow (long context + repeated prefix hits), which increased your per-token bill for a subset of calls.

Quick summary:
- Impact window: 2027-05-24 -> 2027-05-30
- Affected calls: prefetch-enabled /streaming routes for clinical-summarize pipeline
- Observed delta: ~18% increase in egress token counts for the sampled routes (detailed CSV attached)

We are prioritizing a fix in the runtime team; estimated remediation ETA is two weeks (targeting 2027-06-14). Given you’re in production and this is materially outside normal usage patterns, we’d like to propose a short-term commercial smoothing so you aren’t penalized while we stabilize.

Proposed commercial remedy (requesting exec approval):
- 10% bill credit applied to affected line items for the period 2027-05-24 -> 2027-06-13 (to cover until fix + one-week validation)
- One-time invoice adjustment; no change to SOW or base rates

Could you confirm this would help on your side? If yes I’ll loop in Laura and Karthik to coordinate approval and finance flow; I included a small impact CSV and a cost projection in the attachments for your review.

Appreciate the patience — we want to make this right quickly.

Best,
Olga
Olga Petrov
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com
+1 415 555 0198

Attachments: prefetch_prod_impact.csv, cost_projection_q2.xlsx
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Short-term rate smoothing to offset prefetch regression impact

Thanks for raising and for the concise summary, Olga. I reviewed the attachments. A couple notes from a commercial governance perspective:

- We should limit the credit to the specific routes (not account-wide) and to the explicit impact window; the CSV you provided supports that.
- Recommend 10% smoothing as a lower-bound, but given the ~18% measured delta I think we should round to 15% to avoid under-compensating Acme while we validate the fix.
- Term: credit applied retroactively to invoices for 2027-05-24 -> 2027-06-13, captured as a one-line invoice adjustment.

Operational asks for approval path:
1) Exec sign-off (Karthik) for the concession (15% cap, limited window).
2) Finance ops to issue a credit note referencing Deal ACM-4721 and our standard concession rubric.
3) Legal/Contracts to sign off that this is a temporary smoothing, not a rate change (I’ll draft the short amendment).

If Karthik is comfortable I can prepare the wording and the invoice stub; Marcus, can you confirm the finance code we should use for a one-off operational credit?

Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

---
On Tue, Jun 1, 2027 at 09:12 AM Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com> wrote:
> Samantha —
> 
> Thanks again for raising the spike you saw last week. We dug into the logs with infra and confirmed a prefetch optimization we shipped in late May regresses token emission patterns for your workflow...
From: Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@acmehealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Briggs <tom.briggs@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Short-term rate smoothing to offset prefetch regression impact

Olga / Laura —

Thanks for the fast investigation and the clear proposal. We’re impacted on a production schedule so any smoothing that limits surprise billing would be helpful.

We’re OK with a 15% smoothing for the dates you specified, provided we get a short confirmation email / credit note we can attach to our procurement ticket. Two asks from our side:
- Please include the exact routes and invoice line IDs affected so our AP team can reconcile quickly.
- Can we see the SLA amendment draft before it’s finalized?

If you can send the credit note and a one-paragraph amendment I’ll prioritize getting internal PO hold cleared.

Best,
Samantha Cole
Director of Platform Engineering, Acme Health
samantha.cole@acmehealth.com

Attachment: HubSpot deal link (please include in credit note)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: billing@redwood-billing.com
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Short-term rate smoothing to offset prefetch regression impact

All —

Reviewed. Given the measurement and the short remediation ETA I approve a temporary 15% credit for the affected routes and window (2027-05-24 -> 2027-06-13). Conditions:
- Credit limited to the explicit route IDs in the attached CSV.
- One-time invoice adjustment; does not change base pricing or future invoices.
- Finance to issue credit note referencing Deal ACM-4721 and include the HubSpot link.

Marcus — please process as a special credit (use finance code: OP-CRED-EX) and confirm the credit note number when available. Olga/Laura — please share the proposed one-paragraph SLA amendment with Legal for sign-off and send Samantha the credit note stub for AP reconciliation.

Thanks — Karthik
